question: What is the primary objective of the sterilization process?

options.A: Reduction of visible dirt and organic matter from surfaces
options.B: Destruction of vegetative bacteria while leaving spores intact
options.C: Inactivation of common viruses on non-critical furniture
options.D: Complete elimination of all microbial life including spores

explanation: Sterilization is the highest level of microbial control, designed to destroy every living organism and resistant spore present on an object. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is achieving basic cleaning insufficient for surgical instruments entering the bloodstream?

options.A: Cleaning agents leave toxic residues that irritate healthy human tissue
options.B: Residual spores and microorganisms can directly seed severe systemic infections
options.C: Washing processes destroy the metallic integrity of sharp cutting blades
options.D: Blood proteins become permanently bonded to steel during washing

explanation: Instruments breaching sterile tissues require absolute freedom from all microbes to prevent introducing pathogens directly into internal body sites. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which decontamination process must always precede both disinfection and sterilization?
explanation: Organic soil acts as a protective barrier for microorganisms and must be physically washed away before disinfectants or sterilants can work effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h2)

question: What primary feature separates disinfection from sterilization?

options.A: Disinfection is performed exclusively with boiling water
options.B: Disinfection is only used for non-reusable plastic items
options.C: Sterilization completely destroys resistant bacterial spores
options.D: Sterilization requires no prior equipment preparation

explanation: While disinfection eliminates most vegetative pathogens, only true sterilization reliably destroys tough bacterial endospores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which category of instruments requires complete sterilization according to the Spaulding classification?
explanation: Critical items break the skin barrier or enter sterile cavities, carrying the highest risk of infection and requiring full sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing a flexible gastrointestinal endoscope for a patient procedure. Based on the Spaulding classification, how should this device be processed?

options.A: Low-level disinfection using quaternary ammonium compounds
options.B: Simple washing with ordinary tap water and soap
options.C: Immediate high-pressure steam autoclaving for twenty minutes
options.D: High-level disinfection or sterilization due to mucous membrane contact

explanation: Endoscopes touch mucous membranes, classifying them as semi-critical devices that require high-level disinfection or sterilization to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the standard time and temperature combination for gravity displacement steam autoclaving?
explanation: The classic parameters of 121°C, 15 pounds per square inch of pressure, and sufficient time ensure steam penetrates packages and destroys all spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h4)

question: When is dry heat sterilization preferred over steam autoclaving in clinical settings?

options.A: For oils, powders, and moisture-sensitive sharp instruments
options.B: For large bundles of surgical linen and cotton drapes
options.C: For rubber tubing and flexible plastic catheters
options.D: For hollow lumened needles requiring rapid turnaround

explanation: Dry heat does not rust carbon steel and can penetrate non-aqueous powders and oils where steam cannot reach effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which chemical agent is frequently used for liquid immersion sterilization or high-level disinfection of heat-sensitive scopes?
explanation: Glutaraldehyde is a powerful chemical sterilant and disinfectant commonly used for immersible heat-sensitive medical devices. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is a major clinical limitation associated with using liquid chemical sterilants for surgical instruments?

options.A: Items often require sterile rinsing which can re-introduce contaminants if care is lacking
options.B: They demand extreme high-pressure chambers similar to steam autoclaves
options.C: They instantly melt stainless steel surfaces at room temperature
options.D: They require lengthy aeration to eliminate toxic chemical residues

explanation: Unlike terminal steam sterilization inside a sealed wrapper, chemical immersion usually requires rinsing with sterile water post-treatment, risking touch contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which type of monitoring indicator provides direct microbiological proof that sterilization conditions successfully destroyed resistant bacterial spores?
explanation: Biological indicators use actual bacterial spores to test the lethality of the sterilization cycle, offering the highest level of quality assurance. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the limitation of relying solely on external chemical indicator tape on a wrapped instrument pack?

options.A: It can only be read accurately using an ultraviolet laboratory microscope
options.B: It automatically turns black whenever humidity in the room rises above normal levels
options.C: It permanently melts if the autoclave chamber reaches overpressure
options.D: It only proves the exterior was exposed to heat or steam, not that internal items reached required conditions

explanation: Chemical indicator tape confirms exposure to a variable like heat, but it does not guarantee that steam penetrated deep inside the pack to kill all internal spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h6)

question: What modern principle determines whether a stored sterile package is safe to use rather than relying on a fixed calendar expiration date?
explanation: Sterility is maintained based on package handling and environmental integrity (events) rather than the passage of time on a calendar. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h7)

question: A nurse notices that a sterile instrument pack has accidentally fallen onto a damp hospital floor. What action is required?

options.A: Inspect the wrapper for tears, and if intact, use it immediately for the next patient
options.B: Wipe the outer wrapper with alcohol and store it back on the shelf
options.C: Consider the package compromised due to moisture and contamination, requiring complete re-sterilization
options.D: Send the pack directly to the laboratory for biological spore testing

explanation: Moisture allows microorganisms to wick through packaging material via a process called strike-through, rendering the contents unsterile regardless of visual appearance. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h7)
